title: A ZFC counterexample to Naimark's problem
analyst_role: family analyst (paper + Lean); no reasoning trace exists for this family
base_library_L: Mathlib d13f23b + references.bib of this manuscript (14 entries: AkemannWeaver2004, CalderonFarah2022, KishimotoOzawaSakai2003, AkemannAndersonPedersen1986, Kadison1957, BlanchardDykema2001, Ueda2008, UedaPreprint2008, AkemannWassermannWeaver2010, Vaccaro2018, Vaccaro2020, Tanaka2026, FarahHirshberg2017, NaimpallyPeters2013). L contains one 2026 entry, Tanaka2026 (arXiv:2609.26930), which discloses that its construction was developed predominantly by OpenAI ChatGPT.
subject: Operator algebras

main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem}\label{na:main} There exists a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex $C^*$-algebra $A$ with a faithful tracial state such that all its nonzero irreducible representations are unitarily equivalent. In particular, $A$ is not isomorphic to $K(H)$ for any complex Hilbert space $H$. \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: In ZFC there is a unital, simple, infinite-dimensional C*-algebra with a faithful trace and exactly one irreducible representation up to unitary equivalence; being unital and infinite-dimensional it is not K(H). This answers Naimark's 1951 question negatively without diamond (Akemann-Weaver 2004 needed diamond).
main_statement.priority_note: Not the first ZFC answer. Tanaka2026 (arXiv:2609.26930v1, 22 Sep 2026, two days before this preprint) already gives a ZFC counterexample with a faithful tracial state; the paper says so: 'the existence conclusion of Theorem~\ref{na:main} is already present there' (introduction.tex:49-50). This paper is an alternative proof by a different route.

lean_comparator.statement: exists (A : Type u) (_ : CStarAlgebra A), IsSimpleCStar A and not FiniteDimensional C A and (exists tau, IsFaithfulTracialState tau) and HasUniqueIrreducibleRepresentation.{u,v,w} A and forall H : Type v Hilbert, not IsIsomorphicToCompacts A H

IsIrreducible = nonzero and no nontrivial closed invariant subspace (matches introduction.tex:17-18); IsFaithfulTracialState matches introduction.tex:18-19; HasUniqueIrreducibleRepresentation quantifies over Hilbert spaces in arbitrary universes v,w (stronger form of 'all nonzero irreducible representations are unitarily equivalent'); the non-compacts clause is stated for H : Type v, universe-polymorphic. The paper's 'in particular' is proved, not assumed (not_isIsomorphicToCompacts, Recursion.lean:2037).
lean_comparator.formalized_vs_claimed: Everything claimed is formalized, including the cited Kishimoto-Ozawa-Sakai theorem (re-proved, KOS.homogeneity, Operators.lean:927), Kadison transitivity, AAP excision, Ueda's HNN construction and the set-theoretic bookkeeping (constructionCardinal = Order.succ c, Dependencies.lean:425). The algebra is built in Type 0 and lifted with ULift (Tracial.lean:257). D.max_item: T16 the selective bridge (with its analytic core I20); T21 closed-subiteration theorem is the runner-up (N2, borderline N3)

evidence.quote: Then every pure state $h$ of $A$ has a unique state extension

caveats: CF22 Sec. 8 (in L) explicitly proposes this architecture: separable subalgebras that uniquely determine the relevant states, followed by an 'amalgamation' of B x Z with A ('a partial crossed product of sorts', Question 8.1). CF22 Prop 8.3 shows a bridge with (U) for all pure states would give a counterexample under CH. The bridge answers a posed question, so pivot distance may be short.

Ueda's reduced HNN extension is in L; the bridge is an HNN extension along a partial isomorphism of two abelian algebras. The free-product unique-extension technique has a precedent in AWW10 Lemma 0.2.
Tanaka2026 (model-produced) already transports CAR projections of trace 2^-n by KOS automorphisms; only the HNN/bridge and closed-subiteration parts are absent there.

proof_architecture.claim: State tools: excision nets, projection excision, cross-excision, trace-null supports, peaking expectation onto C(N u infty).
Reduced HNN adjunction H(A) as a corner of F*_D G with F=M_2(A), G=M_2(D_1), D=D_1+D_2; expectation onto A; uniqueness by reduced-word trace vanishing; restriction, reordering and limits.

Selective bridge: for matched peaking sequences of inequivalent f_1,f_2, every old pure state extends uniquely and only [f_1],[f_2] merge. Proof: words decay under excision nets via the module bound, endpoint expectations (trace-null at atoms, cross-excision at infinity, Dini), and peak transfer through letters.

Bridge iteration from the CAR algebra with dependency sets; dependency-closed sub-iterations are bridge iterations; closed-subiteration theorem gives (U) for A[S] in X_delta by postponing omitted steps (reordering + no-other-join).
Countable determination: each pure state of X_delta is the unique extension of its pure restriction to a separable A[S]; hence at most c pure states when |delta| <= c.

ZFC recursion of length c^+: a fixed schedule; at stage j, KOS on separable A[S] transports p_n to a matched-trace peaking sequence for the scheduled state, and the bridge joins it to the reference class; countable determination and regularity of c^+ catch every final pure state.
Conclusion: all pure states equivalent, so one irrep; simple, faithful trace, unital and infinite-dimensional, hence not K(H).

lean_route_differences: Amalgamated free product: built on a scalar l^2 Fock space indexed by reduced paths through the atoms of D (AtomicTraceData, AtomicFockSpace; Amalgamation.lean), not on Hilbert C*-modules. Possible because D = C(N u infty) carries atoms of positive trace summing to 1.

KOS homogeneity is re-proved (Homogeneity/Operators/Stages: near-central rows from Krylov projection chains, row-controlled matching, intertwining limit automorphism). An earlier conditional main (main_of_approxNearCentralRows, Recursion.lean:2074) took it as a hypothesis.
Faithfulness of traces is derived from simplicity (tracialState_strictPos_of_simple, Extension.lean:1177) rather than carried.
Endpoints are bundled as a structure (PeakingPairData.Endpoint, Peaking.lean:1645) with a tag recording matched peaks; the paper's case analysis becomes Endpoint.cut / word_decay.

The recursion is a functor-valued transfinite tower (recursiveTower over ConstructionIndex, CategoryTheory.SmallObject.SuccStruct) with ChronologicalHistory carrying active set, dependencies, pairs and 'chronological' ambient presentations.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found on a line-by-line reading of all six sections, and the Lean library proves the comparator statement verbatim with no sorry/axiom/native_decide and with KOS re-proved. Lean was not compiled here. The claim is unrefereed; an independent earlier ZFC construction (Tanaka2026, model-produced) exists, which raises plausibility but is itself unrefereed.
checked: Peaking expectation: continuity at infinity from projection excision; bimodularity via Cauchy-Schwarz at the evaluation character; trace preservation since tau(p_N)->0.
Trace-null supports: r_h u_i* u_j r_h = h(u_i* u_j) r_h = <eta_j, eta_i> r_h = 0 gives m orthogonal translates of trace tau(r_h).
HNN corner: v = e_12^F s is a unitary of e_1 Z e_1 and v p_n^1 v* = p_n^2 because D_2 embeds into G via theta^{-1}; the coefficient table at turns matches the reduced-word conditions.

Bridge endpoint criterion: ||d P_G|| <= ||E_D^F(d*d)||^{1/2}; at a finite atom the limit vanishes by normality and trace-null supports; at infinity it is phi_l(a0* r_h a0), zero unless h = phi_l; Dini gives uniformity because the limit function is 0.

Bridge cases m=1 (double match impossible: s has different range and source), m=2 with both transfers (h=k=phi_i, remaining P_n^j a_1 P_t^j with phi_j(a_1)=0), m>=3 (exposed internal coefficients are centered, so phi_1, phi_2 vanish on them).

Closed-subiteration: O_beta, R_beta are dependency-closed; at active k in S, I_k subset S cap k, so the k-data lie in O_k; three particular states have unique extensions to X_k by peaking-restriction (no circularity); reordering hypotheses (expectations agree by uniqueness of trace-preserving expectations) hold.

Construction step: gamma from KOS on A[S] (simple, separable, infinite-dimensional because it contains A_0); (q_n) peaks to g|A[S] by composing with gamma; T21 lifts peaking to X_j; tau(q_n)=2^-n since gamma(M_{2^n}) is a unital matrix subalgebra.
Final catch: kappa = c^+ regular so countable S is bounded; h|X_beta is pure as a unique extension; sigma(beta,eta) >= beta schedules it.
consistency_checks_passed: AW04 Prop 6: a counterexample needs >= 2^aleph_0 generators. Here the length is c^+, so no conflict, and the paper makes no density claim (introduction.tex:59-61).
AW04 Cor 7 (under not-CH, no aleph_1-generated counterexample): consistent, since nothing here bounds the generators by aleph_1.

Rosenberg / CF22 Prop 7.2: no counterexample has its irreducible representation on a separable space. Here the irreducible representation is nonseparable (it carries c pairwise-distance-2 pure states); the paper explicitly distinguishes this from faithful separable representations (introduction.tex:27-31).
No over-reach: the bridge requires a faithful trace and no f.d. irreps; both are maintained (CAR inside every stage).
